youtube.title: How Credit Card Companies Make Money Off You
youtube.description:
How do credit card companies make money? Three ways: swipe fees on every purchase, interest on the balance you carry, and penalty fees. We break down the real numbers, show why paying only the minimum on a $5,000 balance can take about 19 years, and give you 5 moves to make your card company earn nothing from you.

Numbers in this video
• Average credit card APR on accounts assessed interest: 22.36% in Q3 2026 (preliminary), commercial banks (Federal Reserve G.19 Consumer Credit, released Nov 6, 2026)
• U.S. credit card balances: $1.29 trillion in Q3 2026, up $22 billion in the quarter (New York Fed, Household Debt and Credit Report, Nov 10, 2026)
• Card interest charged to consumers: about $160 billion in 2024, up from $105 billion in 2022; fees $31.3 billion in 2024, including $17 billion in late fees and $8.7 billion in annual fees; average APR margin over prime a record 16.4 points in 2024; about 15% of general purpose cardholders paid only the minimum; about half of accounts revolve a balance (CFPB, The Consumer Credit Card Market report, Dec 2025)
• Merchant card processing fees in 2025: about $198 billion (Nilson Report) to $251 billion (CMSPI estimate); Visa and Mastercard credit fees averaged about 2.4% to 2.9% of the purchase (as reported via the Merchants Payments Coalition, Nov 2026)
• Minimum payment example is an illustration: $5,000 at 22.36% APR, minimum = 1% of balance + monthly interest ($25 floor), no new charges. Minimum only: about 231 months and about $8,240 in interest. $200 a month: 34 months and about $1,790. Your card's formula may differ.
• "About 10% a year" for stocks is a commonly quoted long-run average, not a guarantee.
